correctness.rationale: PASS. Distinguished the purely combinatorial quantifier (for every ordered triple of unordered nonempty three-block partitions, existence of pairwise-disjoint transversal) from the valuation-space implication (failure of MMS forces every chosen MMS partition triple to be exceptional, not that an exceptional triple suffices for every arbitrary valuation profile). For five goods, partition types are (3,1,1) and (2,2,1). Reconstructed the case split by singleton coincidences, Hall's theorem when three singleton choices can be distinct, and the unique residual matchings-on-four argument. Independently implemented the exact set-partition enumeration using surjection-generated frozensets, not the supplied bitmask source: 25 three-partitions, 15,625 ordered triples, exactly 30 lacking a transversal; equivalence with the stated common-singleton/three-matching normal form holds for every triple, and all 6^3 four-good triples admit a transversal. For the explicit binary monotone valuation, the common good or complete pair in each agent's private matching has value one; disjoint matching pairs of distinct matchings intersect, so no exact MMS allocation. Sharpness extends to <=4 goods with nonnegative monotone valuations. The census is exhaustive after proved finite reduction, not extrapolation of a partial sample. Not a classification of all valuation functions.

originality.rationale: PASS, qualified best-of-knowledge. Prior small-hypergraph rainbow matching lemmas or unindexed enumeration could overlap and are recorded as risks. Negative searches alone do not establish priority.
